paras: On Oct 12, the Bank of Russia confirmed in an updated FAQ that direct crypto trades between individuals stay legal <g>only until July 1, 2027.</g>
<u>After that, every trade has to go through a broker or exchange on the central bank's register.</u>
The rules come from Russia's new crypto law, which took effect on Sept 1.

items.l: yearly buy cap for non-qualified investors (~$3,600)
coins they can buy: BTC, ETH, USDT

slides.source: Bank of Russia FAQ via Decrypt, Cointelegraph

paras: Since Binance sold its Russian business in 2023, P2P has been a go-to way to get stablecoins: <g>wire rubles to a seller's card, receive USDT.</g>
The new rules also block moving crypto from a licensed account to <r>your own wallet.</r>
Paying for goods and services in crypto stays banned. Foreign trade settlements in crypto are allowed.
And the banks are moving in: <g>Sberbank</g> joined the central bank's register on Oct 12.
Industry voices say P2P is <g>harder to shut down</g> than any exchange, and that the rules may be tough to enforce.
<u>The goal is clear: every ruble-to-crypto trade on rails the state can see.</u>
<r>The open question: do users move onto licensed rails, or further off the grid?</r>
